# Statedoku

> Statedoku is a free daily US geography puzzle: a 3×3 grid where every cell must hold a US state that satisfies both its row clue and its column clue. The site also has 21 free geography games (map clicking, capitals, abbreviations, flags, history) and reference pages on the 50 states, in English, French and Spanish. Free, no signup.

Last updated: 2026-10-15. Online since May 2026; daily puzzles since 1 June 2026. Statedoku is made by Moses Tounby. That is a pen name for a solo developer based in France. It is an independent project with no company, team or investor behind it, and it is not affiliated with the New York Times, Wordle or any publisher.

## Answers

**What is Statedoku?** A daily logic puzzle about US geography at https://statedoku.com. Each cell of a 3×3 grid needs a US state that matches two clues at once, for example "Borders Canada" and "No state income tax" (Alaska, New Hampshire and Washington fit).

**How many mistakes are allowed?** Five per puzzle.

**When does a new puzzle appear?** At midnight in the player's local time. Everyone playing the same date gets the same grid.

**Is only one answer accepted per cell?** No. Any state that satisfies both clues is accepted. Filled cells stay editable, since a state placed early may be needed elsewhere.

**Is it free?** Yes. No signup, no download, no account. An optional daily email reminder needs a confirmed address.

**What else is there to play?** 21 free games, each in English, French and Spanish, listed below. Most deal a fresh random round each time and score from 1 to 3 stars.

**Can teachers use it?** Yes. The daily puzzle and every game page have a "Share to Google Classroom" button, the games can be embedded in an iframe (https://statedoku.com/widgets/), and there is a free printable map. Students need no account.

**How is it different from Wordle or Worldle?** Wordle is about words and Worldle about country shapes. Statedoku is a logic grid where each answer is a US state matching two written clues.

## The daily puzzle

- [Daily puzzle in English](https://statedoku.com/): Statedoku is a free daily geography puzzle. Fill a 3×3 grid with US states that satisfy every row and column constraint.
- [Puzzle quotidien en français](https://statedoku.com/fr/): Statedoku est un puzzle géographique quotidien gratuit. Remplissez une grille 3×3 d'États américains qui respectent chaque contrainte de ligne et de colonne.
- [Puzzle diario en español](https://statedoku.com/es/): Statedoku es un puzzle de geografía diario y gratis. Rellena una cuadrícula 3×3 con estados de EE.UU. que cumplan cada restricción de fila y columna.
- [How to Play Statedoku, Daily US States Puzzle Rules & Tips](https://statedoku.com/how-to-play/): Learn how to play Statedoku, the daily US states puzzle. Rules, tips, scoring, and a full walkthrough of the 3×3 geography grid with constraint examples.
- [Statedoku Archive, Play Past Daily Puzzles](https://statedoku.com/archive/): Browse and play every past Statedoku puzzle. Each date has its own unique 3×3 US states grid. Tap any day on the calendar to play that puzzle.
- [Statedoku FAQ, Daily US Geography Puzzle](https://statedoku.com/faq/): Common questions about Statedoku: how it works, is it free, why a new puzzle every day, mobile support, difference from Wordle and Sudoku, and more.

## 21 free geography games

Each game exists in English, French and Spanish: replace /play/ with /fr/play/ or /es/play/.

- [All 21 games](https://statedoku.com/play/): 21 free games to learn all 50 US states: placement on the map, capitals, abbreviations, flags, history, electoral college, time zones and more. EN/FR/ES.
- [Place the State](https://statedoku.com/play/place-the-state/): Click the named state on a blank US map. Easy (5 well-known states), Normal (10) or Hard (15, lookalikes included), 3 lives.
- [USPS Abbreviations Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-abbreviations/): Match the 2-letter postal code to its US state. 20 rounds, multiple choice.
- [State Capitals Match](https://statedoku.com/play/state-capitals-match/): Match 10 US states with their capitals.
- [State Silhouettes](https://statedoku.com/play/state-silhouettes/): Guess the US state from its outline alone.
- [States Connections](https://statedoku.com/play/states-connections/): NYT-Connections style: group 16 US states into 4 hidden categories.
- [State Capitals Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-capitals-typing/): Type the capital of each US state.
- [Biggest City Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/biggest-cities/): Identify the biggest city of each US state.
- [State Flags Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-flags/): Identify a state from its flag description.
- [13 Original Colonies](https://statedoku.com/play/thirteen-colonies/): Click all 13 original American colonies on the US map.
- [State Admission Order](https://statedoku.com/play/state-admission-order/): Order 8 states by their year of admission to the Union.
- [Confederate States Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/confederate-states/): Click all 11 Confederate states of the US Civil War on the map.
- [Presidents by State](https://statedoku.com/play/president-birth-states/): Match US presidents to their state of birth.
- [State Nicknames Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-nicknames/): Match nicknames to their states: Lone Star, Golden State, Sunshine State.
- [State Mottos Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-mottos/): Match each state to its official motto.
- [State Symbols Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/state-symbols/): Match state birds, flowers, and trees to their US state.
- [Time Zones Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/time-zones/): Identify the time zone of each US state.
- [Border States Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/border-states/): Click all states bordering Canada or Mexico on the US map.
- [Rivers & Mountains](https://statedoku.com/play/rivers-mountains/): Match US rivers and mountain landmarks to their states.
- [Electoral College Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/electoral-college/): Test how many electoral votes each state has.
- [Swing States Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/swing-states/): Click all 7 swing states of 2024 on the US map.
- [No Income Tax Quiz](https://statedoku.com/play/no-income-tax-states/): Click all 9 US states with no state income tax.

## For teachers

- [Embeddable US States Quizzes](https://statedoku.com/widgets/): Free embeddable US-states quizzes you can drop into any classroom blog, LMS or learning site. Copy the iframe code, no signup, no fee.
- [Free Printable US States Map, Blank & Labeled PDFs](https://statedoku.com/learn/printable-us-states-map/): Free printable US states maps for teachers and parents. Blank map for quizzes, labeled map with state codes, plus a reference table. Press Ctrl+P.
- [US States Quiz, Quick Test of All 50 States & Capitals](https://statedoku.com/quiz/): Free 10-question US states quiz. Test your knowledge of all 50 state names, capitals, and regions. Mobile-friendly, no signup, instant scoring.

## Reference pages

- [How to Learn the 50 US States (Fast), A Free Method](https://statedoku.com/learn/): Learn all 50 US states by region in under a week. A method built on grouping, geography, and daily practice, no flashcards.
- [All 50 States in the USA (Map, Capitals, Facts)](https://statedoku.com/states/): All 50 states in the USA on one clickable map, from Alabama to Wyoming. Tap any state for its capital, nickname, population, history, and fun facts.
- [US Regions & Subregions, All 13 Census Areas](https://statedoku.com/regions/): The 4 US regions and 9 subregions as defined by the US Census Bureau. Browse states by region. Region members, sub-regions, key facts, and a clickable map.
- [Top 100 US Cities by Population, 2024 Census Estimates](https://statedoku.com/cities/): The 100 most populous US cities, ranked by the Census Bureau's July 1, 2024 population estimates, with the state each city belongs to.
- [Fun Facts About All 50 US States 🇺🇸](https://statedoku.com/facts/): A curated collection of weird, surprising, and verified fun facts about each of the 50 US states.
- [All 50 US States and Capitals (Full A to Z List)](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-and-capitals/): All 50 US states and their capitals, listed A to Z from Alabama (Montgomery) to Wyoming (Cheyenne), with statehood year, abbreviation, and region.
- [How to Memorize All 50 US State Capitals (Fast)](https://statedoku.com/learn/state-capitals/): Memorize all 50 US state capitals in under a week. Region-by-region breakdown, mnemonic tricks for the trickiest ones (Boise, Pierre, Topeka), and a daily game.
- [All 50 US State Abbreviations (2-Letter Codes)](https://statedoku.com/learn/state-abbreviations/): All 50 US state abbreviations in one alphabetical list, each with its capital. Plus a memory trick and the handful of two-letter codes people mix up most often.
- [13 Original Colonies in Order: Full List, Map, Dates](https://statedoku.com/learn/13-colonies/): The 13 original colonies became the first 13 states, from Delaware (ratified 1787) to Rhode Island (1790). Full list in order, with capitals and a map.
- [Electoral College Votes by State (Updated)](https://statedoku.com/learn/electoral-college/): How many electoral college votes each US state has, why it matters, and how it shaped recent elections.
- [The 11 Confederate States in Order of Secession](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-confederate/): The 11 states that left the Union in 1860-61 to form the Confederacy. South Carolina went first, North Carolina last, exact dates and what triggered each.
- [The 4 US Regions Explained, Census Map](https://statedoku.com/learn/us-regions/): The official US Census Bureau divides the country into 4 regions and 9 subregions. Learn which states are in each, why the divisions matter, and memory tricks.
- [Largest & Smallest US States by Area (Ranked 1 to 50)](https://statedoku.com/learn/largest-states/): All 50 US states ranked by area. Alaska is biggest (#1, 663k sq mi), Rhode Island is smallest (#50). Includes top 10 + bottom 10 tables and an interactive map.
- [The 13 US states that border Canada](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-bordering-canada/): The 13 US states that share a border with Canada. Alaska has the longest at 1,538 mi, Michigan the longest in the lower 48, Pennsylvania the shortest.
- [The 4 US states that border Mexico](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-bordering-mexico/): Just 4 US states border Mexico, California, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas. Border miles per state, busiest crossings, and the cities you'd never expect.
- [20 Landlocked US States and the Doubly Landlocked Ones](https://statedoku.com/learn/landlocked-states/): The 20 landlocked US states, with no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shore. Full list with capitals and regions, a map, and what doubly landlocked means.
- [The 9 US states with no state income tax](https://statedoku.com/learn/no-income-tax/): The 9 US states with no state income tax in 2026, Alaska, Florida, Nevada, NH, SD, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming. Plus the catch in each one.
- [US States by GDP, Ranking of all 50 economies (2026)](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-by-gdp-ranking/): The full ranking of US states by GDP. California $4.25T, Texas $2.90T, New York $2.47T, Florida $1.83T. How each state compares, and what drives the gap.
- [House Seats by State, 1910 to 2020](https://statedoku.com/learn/house-seats-by-state-1910-2020/): Every state's US House seats at each census from 1910 to 2020, from Census Bureau data: who gained, who lost, and how the South and West overtook the North.
- [All 50 US state nicknames, official + popular (2026)](https://statedoku.com/learn/state-nicknames-complete/): The complete list of nicknames for all 50 US states. Texas is the Lone Star State, California the Golden State, Florida the Sunshine State.
- [US Presidents and the States Where They Were Born](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-presidents-born/): All 45 US presidents (47 presidencies) and their birth states. Virginia leads with 8 presidents. Learn US geography step by step with maps, lists, and trivia.
- [Every State Flower and the Meaning Behind It](https://statedoku.com/learn/state-flowers/): The official flower of all 50 US states, when each was adopted, what it symbolizes, and the surprising stories behind the picks (yes, even the cactus).
- [Which 8 States Touch the Great Lakes?](https://statedoku.com/learn/states-with-great-lakes/): Eight US states share shoreline with the Great Lakes, Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario. Mapped by lake, with miles of coastline per state.

## Quick facts

- 50 states. Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.
- 13 states border Canada: Alaska, Idaho, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, New Hampshire, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Vermont, Washington.
- 4 states border Mexico: Arizona, California, New Mexico, Texas.
- 17 state capitals are also their state's largest city.
- 9 states levy no broad personal income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming.
- 20 states have no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shore.
- The Census Bureau groups the states into 4 regions: Northeast (9), South (16), Midwest (12) and West (13).
